{{nihongo|'''Naka Shrine (Matsuzaki)'''|仲神社 (松崎町)}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Izu Province]].

Its former rank was the village shrine of Naka Village in former {{ill|Naka district|Q11642882|qid=Q11642882|lt=Naka District}}.

=== Enshrined deities ===
; Main deity
* {{ill|Kotoshironushi-no-Mikoto|lt=Kotoshironushi|Q8009611|qid=Q8009611|qid=Q8009611|lt=Kotoshironushi-no-Mikoto}}
; Associated hall deity
* {{ill|Sugawara no Michizane|Q382005|qid=Q382005}}
According to the Edo-period {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō Studies|ja|神名帳考証|qid=Q11588824}}, the main deity was then different from today, being "{{ill|Utsushi Hikanasaku no Mikoto|fr|Utsushihikanasaku|ja|宇都志日金拆命|qid=Q86736058|lt=Utsushinaga-no-Mikoto}}<ref>said to be connected to the {{ill|Azumi people|fr|Peuple Azumi|id|Suku Azumi|it|Azumi (popolo)|ja|阿曇氏|ko|아즈미씨|ru|Адзуми (народ)|simple|Azumi people|qid=Q3377806|lt=Azumi}}.</ref>"<ref>[https://kokusho.nijl.ac.jp/biblio/100132933/230?ln=ja Jinmyōchō Kōshō] (leaf 230)</ref>. The associated deity {{ill|Sugawara no Michizane|Q382005|qid=Q382005}} had been enshrined at Tsushima Shrine in the precincts, but was merged into the main shrine before {{ill|Bunroku|Q1373039|qid=Q1373039}}.

=== Origin ===
The foundation period is unknown. It is said that "Naka" in the name changed from "Naga" of Naga-gō in {{ill|Naka district|Q11642882|qid=Q11642882|lt=Naka District}}.

In the medieval period it was merged into Inakami Shrine and called "Takane Myōjin."<ref>Old Nakagawa Village shrine/temple detailed ledger (published Taishō 15)</ref>
In {{ill|Bunroku|Q1373039|qid=Q1373039}} 2 (1593), it was re-established at the present former site and resumed the name "Naka Shrine."

In August of {{ill|Meiji era|ar|فترة مييجي|ast|Dómina Meiji|az|Meydzi dövrü|azb|مئی‌جی دؤورو|be|Перыяд Мэйдзі|bn|মেইজি যুগ|bo|མེའི་ཇིའི་དུས་དུས་མཚམས།|ca|Era Meiji|cs|Období Meidži|da|Meiji-perioden|de|Meiji-Zeit|el|Μεϊτζί (περίοδος)|es|Era Meiji|et|Meiji periood|eu|Meiji Aroa|fa|دوره میجی|fi|Meiji-kausi|fr|Ère Meiji|gl|Período Meiji|he|תקופת מייג'י|hr|Meiji (razdoblje)|ht|Epòk Meiji|hu|Meidzsi-kor|id|Zaman Meiji|io|Ero Meiji|is|Meiji-tímabilið|it|Periodo Meiji|ja|明治|ka|მეიძის ეპოქა|kbp|Mejii wɛɛ yaa alɩwaatʊ|kk|Мэйдзи дәуірі|ko|메이지 시대|la|Aetas Meiji|lt|Meidži laikotarpis|lv|Meidzi periods|mk|Меиџи (период)|mn|Мэйжийн эрин|ms|Zaman Meiji|nl|Meijiperiode|nn|Meiji|no|Meiji-perioden|pl|Meiji (okres)|pt|Era Meiji|ro|Perioada Meiji|ru|Мэйдзи|simple|Meiji period|sk|Obdobie Meidži|sq|Periudha Meixhi|sr|Меиџи период|sv|Meijiperioden|ta|மெய்சி காலம்|th|ยุคเมจิ|tl|Panahong Meiji|tr|Meiji Dönemi|uk|Період Мейдзі|ur|میجی دور|vi|Thời kỳ Minh Trị|war|Panahon Meiji|wuu|明治|zh|明治|zh_classical|明治|zh_min_nan|Bêng-tī|zh_yue|明治|qid=Q3125096}} 6 (1873), it was promoted to village shrine.
On August 14, {{ill|Shōwa era|ar|فترة شووا|br|Oadvezh Shōwa|ca|Període Shōwa|cs|Období Šówa|de|Shōwa-Zeit|eo|Ŝova-epoko|es|Era Shōwa|eu|Shōwa aroa|fa|دوره شووا|fi|Shōwa-kausi|fr|Ère Shōwa (1926-1989)|he|תקופת שווה|hi|शोवा युग|hu|Sóva-kor|id|Zaman Shōwa|it|Periodo Shōwa|ja|昭和|ka|შოვას პერიოდი|ko|쇼와 시대|lt|Šiova laikotarpis|ms|Zaman Shōwa|nl|Showaperiode|no|Shōwa-perioden|pl|Shōwa|pt|Período Shōwa|ru|Сёва|simple|Shōwa era|sr|Шова период|sv|Shōwa|th|ยุคโชวะ|tl|Panahong Shōwa|tr|Şova Dönemi|uk|Період Сьова|vi|Thời kỳ Chiêu Hòa|zh|昭和|zh_classical|昭和|zh_min_nan|Chiau-hô|zh_yue|昭和|qid=Q327567}} 34 (1958), a typhoon destroyed the shrine buildings, but in the following year the haiden, cover hall, and torii were rebuilt in concrete.
The Naka Life Improvement Center in the precincts is used as a meeting hall.

=== Sessha and massha ===
* Tsushima Shrine (merged into the main shrine)

=== Festivals ===
* Spring festival (February 11)
* Tsushima Shrine annual festival day (July 15)
* Hassaku festival (September 1)
* Autumn festival (November 3)
